title: Lebesgue integral and positive and negative parts
terms: Lebesgue integral; Lebesgue integrable function; positive part; negative part; absolute integrability.

question.text:
R
A nonnegative measurable function f on [0, 1] satisfies f dm = 0. Which conclusion must
hold?
(A) f(x) = 0 for every x.
(B) f is bounded.
(C) {x : f(x) > 0} has measure zero.
(D) f is continuous.
(E) {x : f(x) > 0} is countable.

solution.text:
R
−1
For each positive integer k, nonnegativity gives 0 = f ≥ k m({f ≥ 1/k}), so each such
level set is null. Their countable union is {f > 0} and is null. A function can nevertheless
be nonzero on an uncountable null set, or have arbitrarily large finite values at a countable
set of points.
